current.text: Isaiah Stewart has been traded, so Reed is Detroit's backup center behind Jalen Duren.
The projected bench order is Isaiah Joe as sixth man, then Ron Holland, Reed and Daniss Jenkins.
Duren has not played in preseason. Reed has started every Pistons preseason game.
Reed has looked very good in preseason and should be useful this season.
Duren may be eased in, which would give Reed more minutes early in the season.
current.until: Duren is eased into full minutes

current.text: Duren's signing caps Reed's upside. If Duren plays about 28 minutes, Reed should play about 20.
If Duren misses time and Reed plays about 28 minutes, he could be a top 40 to 50 player.
Experts take him late, around pick 120 to 140 or round 13. One expert says pick 108 is too early.
Josh likes Reed a lot and thinks he has enough standalone value as a late pick.
Detroit is projected to win 50 to 51 games and finish third or fourth in the East.

durable.text: He is an excellent per-minute producer.
He is not built to carry a 30-minute starter's load.
He has always posted a high block rate per possession. 29% of his rim contests become blocks.
He makes almost no threes, which is weak even for a big.

note: Reed is a cheap late flyer. Yahoo (rank 189) and ESPN (rank 242) both price him at 0 USD, and experts take him around pick 120 to 140, which is the last rounds of our 144-player draft, so 1 to 2 USD is the right price. He fits punt 3PM builds and adds FG% on low volume, steals, blocks and few turnovers in about 20 minutes. Early in the season, watch how fast Duren's minutes ramp up, because Reed's value as a starter is much higher than his value as a backup.
